title: Does N-acetylcysteine lower blood lead in exposed workers?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.outcome: Blood lead in workers who remain exposed
grade.basis: One randomized, unblinded, no-placebo study reporting change from baseline.

answerHtml: In 171 men with ongoing occupational lead exposure, blood lead fell from baseline in groups assigned to N-acetylcysteine for 12 weeks. Erythrocyte glutathione rose 5 percent and 6 percent at 400 and 800 mg/day. There was no placebo, blinding was not stated, and exposure continued. No glutathione trial with a metal outcome was located. Glutathione is graded on its own page.

sections.heading: Study
sections.html: Kasperczyk and colleagues (2013) randomized 171 workers, 49 of them controls, to no treatment or one of three doses. doi:10.3109/15563650.2013.802797. PMID 23731375. Later papers from the same group were not counted as independent trials.
